title: Global Sugar Balance Outlook — Q2 202666
shortDescription: 666A structured view of supply-demand balance in major sugar corridors and implications for institutional procurement windows.
body:
## Executive Summary66

Global sugar markets remain supported by disciplined export flows and firm destination demand across MENA and Asia.

For institutional buyers, procurement timing continues to matter more than spot-price volatility. Forward visibility on vessel allocation, quality tolerances, and counterparty readiness can materially improve execution outcomes.

## Key Market Signals

- Export programs in key origins remain active but tightly scheduled.
- Refinery demand in destination markets is stable, with intermittent restocking cycles.
- Freight remains a meaningful component of total landed cost.

## Institutional Implications

AFGT continues to observe stronger outcomes where buyers combine volume planning with pre-aligned logistical terms. The practical priority is execution certainty rather than nominal spot advantage.

## Outlook

Near-term market structure suggests selective procurement windows rather than broad-based easing. Institutional participants should retain optionality across origin mix and delivery windows.
